summary.headline: The Select Board reviewed Route 9 wastewater financing, evaluated OPEB liabilities, approved two town financial policies, and extended the wastewater committee charge.
summary.summary: The Select Board met to hear an actuarial presentation on Southborough's Other Post-Employment Benefits (OPEB) funding status and explored long-term contribution strategies. The board also received a progress report from the Regional Wastewater Planning Committee on a potential $40 million to $50 million Route 9 sewer system, voting to extend the committee's charge through June 2027. Additionally, the board adopted an updated Senior Tax Work-Off Policy, approved a comprehensive Grants Management Policy, and signed the Annual Town Election warrant.

topics.title: Pole petition for 361 Turnpike Road
topics.summary: The board opened a public hearing on a joint petition from Massachusetts Electric Company and National Grid to install a new utility pole at 361 Turnpike Road. A National Grid representative explained the new pole is needed to provide electric service to a new commercial building for Valvoline.
key_details: Petition requested installation of pole 43-1 across the street to serve 361 Turnpike Road.
The pole provides direct electric service for a newly constructed commercial facility.
No public opposition or questions were raised during the hearing.
topics.outcome: Approved following the close of the public hearing.

topics.title: OPEB actuarial valuation and funding strategy
topics.summary: Linda Bournival of KMS Actuaries presented an educational overview of the town's Other Post-Employment Benefits (OPEB) liability, trust assets, and discount rates. The board discussed Southborough's funded ratio compared to neighboring communities and considered long-term funding strategies, including the possibility of redirecting pension catch-up appropriations toward OPEB once the Worcester Regional Retirement System reaches full funding around 2036.
key_details: Southborough currently appropriates $250,000 annually into its OPEB trust fund in addition to pay-as-you-go retiree health premiums.
The town's OPEB trust fund holds approximately $4.5 million, reflecting a funded ratio of roughly 8 percent.
Worcester Regional Retirement assessments currently increase about 10 to 11.7 percent annually and are scheduled to be fully funded by 2036.
When the regional retirement system is fully funded, approximately $7.5 million in annual catch-up payments could theoretically become available for reallocation.
Actuaries will model various scenario projections, such as aiming for an 80 percent or 100 percent funded status by target years.
topics.outcome: Discussion only; the board agreed to have the actuary model multiple future contribution scenarios.
topics.why_it_matters: OPEB obligations represent tens of millions of dollars in unfunded municipal liabilities that directly influence the town's bond ratings and long-term tax requirements.

topics.title: Route 9 wastewater system update and committee extension
topics.summary: The Regional Wastewater Planning Committee presented a status report on plans to establish a municipal wastewater system serving the Route 9 commercial corridor. Committee members discussed technical requirements, including an estimated project cost between $40 million and $50 million, the need for a 15- to 20-acre leaching area, and a proposed District Improvement Financing (DIF) plan targeted for the fall Special Town Meeting.
key_details: The projected system requires handling 300,000 to 500,000 gallons per day to support Route 9 commercial development.
Total estimated project capital cost is between $40 million and $50 million, modeled after Littleton's recent system.
Because EPA rules prevent new surface water discharge into local rivers, the town must locate 15 to 20 acres for ground discharge leaching fields.
The proposed DIF district would span roughly 1,600 acres across 600 parcels with an existing assessed value of about $800 million, capturing incremental tax revenue to pay debt service.

The town missed out on a state One Stop grant because the project lacked a secured site and advanced engineering, prompting the committee to consider seeking design funds at fall Special Town Meeting.
topics.outcome: The board voted 4-0-1 to extend the charge of the Regional Wastewater Planning Committee through June 30, 2027.
topics.why_it_matters: A $40 million to $50 million Route 9 wastewater system would unlock commercial development along the highway and would require voter approval for a special property tax allocation district.

topics.title: Town administrative and committee reports
topics.summary: The board heard updates regarding community services, health insurance open enrollment, and regional emergency dispatch. The town administrator noted the regional dispatch district is preparing for short-term bond financing to fund construction, while a board member reported that open enrollment includes a high-deductible health plan that could generate substantial municipal savings if adopted widely.
key_details: Margery Coldwell retired after 25 years as volunteer coordinator of the Southborough Food Pantry and was recognized with a town proclamation.
Health insurance open enrollment for FY27 starts in May, with an employee health fair scheduled for Wednesday, May 6, from 1:00 p.m. to 4:00 p.m. at the Senior Center.
Southborough Town Scholarship applications are due to the Building Department by Thursday, May 7, at 4:00 p.m.

The Regional Emergency Communication Center (RECC) Board of Directors hired bond counsel and a financial advisor to prepare a short-term bond issuance ahead of a July 1 construction start and an anticipated October 2027 operational date.
Any RECC bond issuance must be formally recommended by its finance committee and approved by each member town's select board.
topics.outcome: Informational updates; no formal votes required.

topics.title: Routine business
topics.summary: The board addressed regular administrative matters, including consent agenda approvals, edits to past meeting minutes, an administrative staff appointment, and signing the election warrant. Board members clarified that $25 million in infrastructure borrowing on the election ballot was divided into two distinct debt exclusion questions separating road paving from sidewalk projects.
key_details: Approved the appointment of a business administrator for Youth and Family Services.
Approved consent agenda items B, C, F, and G.
Approved amended meeting minutes for March 31, 2026, and April 7, 2026.
Approved the warrant for the 2026 Annual Town Election.
Clarified that the election ballot will feature four debt exclusion questions, including separate questions for four specific sidewalk projects and a multi-year road repair program.

topics.title: Senior Tax Work-Off and Grants Management policies
topics.summary: The board reviewed and adopted two financial policies. Revisions to the Senior Tax Work-Off Policy updated eligibility rules and expanded the program to 40 positions, while a newly drafted Grants Management Policy established municipal oversight and approval procedures to ensure grants do not create unfunded operating expenses or ongoing personnel costs.
key_details: The Senior Tax Work-Off Policy was updated to remove specific dollar figures, allow income-eligible participants from other programs to automatically qualify, and eliminate an age-18 restriction for designated helpers.
The board set the authorized number of Senior Tax Work-Off participant positions at 40, up from the previous cap of 30.
The new Grants Management Policy establishes a tracking sheet managed by the town accountant for all grant applications and awards.

Grants that require town matching funds, create ongoing full-time equivalent (FTE) personnel, impact employee benefits, or require capital purchases over $10,000 must receive advance approval from the Select Board or School Committee.
topics.outcome: The Senior Tax Work-Off Policy and 40-slot allocation were approved unanimously; the Grants Management Policy was approved unanimously with minor clerical corrections.

votes.motion: Close the public hearing on the pole petition for 361 Turnpike Road
Approve the pole petition for installation of a new pole at 361 Turnpike Road
Approve the appointment of the Youth and Family Services Business Administrator
Extend the charge of the Regional Wastewater Planning Committee to June 30, 2027
Approve consent agenda items B, C, F, and G
Approve the warrant for the 2026 Annual Town Election
Accept the revised Senior Tax Work-Off Policy
Set the number of available positions under the Senior Tax Work-Off Policy at 40
Approve the Grants Management Financial Policy as amended
